claims.text: Introducing nanoprecipitates into fcc FeCoNi can increase its coercive field beyond 100 Oe.
The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
Suitable alloy composition, temperature, and processing conditions can facilitate nanoprecipitate formation.
Nanoprecipitates act as domain-wall pinning sites in fcc FeCoNi.
Domain-wall pinning by nanoprecipitates increases the coercive field.
FeCoNi containing nanoprecipitates will have a coercive field above 100 Oe and higher than a matched material without nanoprecipitates.
The relevant magnetic measurements are to be performed below the Curie temperature.
Processing can both maintain a single-phase fcc structure and facilitate nanoprecipitate formation.
Nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and composition affect the magnitude of coercivity enhancement.

contradictions.description: Introducing nanoprecipitates normally implies formation of a compositionally or structurally distinct precipitate phase, while the boundary simultaneously requires maintenance of a single-phase fcc structure. The hypothesis does not explain how both conditions can hold.
